h: Shabbos Peace Reveals How All Creation Becomes Very Good

p: "I will grant peace in the land" (Vayikra 26:6).
'If there is no peace, there is nothing';
From here we learn that peace
Now, what proof does this bring
that it is equal to everything?
do we say it as it is written?
And why did the Men of the Great Assembly change
for the sake of a refined expression?
But it is brought in sefarim
in the name of our holy master,
רַבִּי ר׳ בֶּער זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
Rebbi R' Ber, zecher tzaddik livrachah:
"And of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil"
from where does evil have existence?
After all, we do not find
the creation of evil in the world.
(פְּסָחִים נד, א; וּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד)
מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא כְּתִיב טוֹב בַּשֵּׁנִי
"Why is 'good' not written on the second day?
Because Gehinnom was created on it."
And also of the first utterance,
"'In the beginning' is also an utterance"
גַּם כֵּן לֹא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ כִּי טוֹב
there too "that it was good" is not written.
"'Also to punish the righteous is not good'
'not good' means nothing other than evil";
and because "that it was good" was not written,
from this evil came into existence.
"And the earth was formless and void, and darkness";
these are the deeds of the wicked";
that it alludes to the four kingdoms;
and this too is the darkness and the evil
that was created on the first day.
And the reason it is not written explicitly
HaKadosh Baruch Hu did not create
was not created to do evil,
I created Torah as its antidote"
(in the Gemara and in Bereishis Rabbah there):
He included it on the sixth day,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹקִים אֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
'And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good.'"
and then there is no evil at all in the world,
for even the yetzer hara and Gehinnom
כִּי קוֹדֶם לָזֶה נֶאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים לח, ד)
"There is no peace in my bones
and only after everything has been rectified
And this is what they said:
"and we say 'everything,' as a refined expression"
to allude to what it says,
"And He saw, etc., all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good";
that out of the evil comes "very good."
And this is what the verse says:
"I will grant peace in the land,
and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid";
for we find the language of fear
with Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him
because of fear in the nights";
and this means the harmful spirits and the yetzer hara.
And about this HaKadosh Baruch Hu
meaning that you will not fear
"and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid, etc."
that they will no longer need protection,
which is the close of Shabbos,
that He whose is the peace
will place upon us blessing and peace
that is, the spreading of the shelter of peace
that is over us on Shabbos,
and we draw this upon ourselves
הִיא נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
so that it be lasting and fixed
for his middah is the middah of truth,
"The lip of truth shall be established forever."
